Aegion is an ESA BIC UK supported advanced materials venture headquartered at Space Park Leicester, UK. We are dedicated to the development and qualification of high-performance materials designed to withstand the harshest frontiers of space exploration and deep-tech industry
Aegion operates at the intersection of metallurgy and aerospace engineering, delivering solutions for environments where traditional materials fail. entityDescription:
UWRC sp. z o.o. (UWRC Ltd) established in 2012, is the special purpose vehicle (spv) of the University of Warsaw (UW), Poland, which is a sole shareholder of the company. The UWRC Ltd was established to support University researchers and students in indirect commercialization of their scientific activity results (setting up spin-off companies). The company is established to comply with Polish Higher Education and Research legal framework, which allows universities to setup companies and hold shares only through the spv.
The UWRC Ltd offers to students and faculty members a range of services from mentoring, business idea assessment, definition of value proposition, business model development, market validation, monetisation strategies, etc. Since establishment in 2012 the UWRC Ltd supported setting up of more than 30 university based, deep-tech spin-off companies. At present the UWRC Ltd manages a portfolio of more than 20 spin-offs.
The UWRC Ltd offers also to UW students and researchers the preincubation services. It allows sciencepreneurs to develop Proof of Concepts, MVPs and test the market with their early products and services under an umbrella of UWRC Ltd legal entity, without taking a risk of setting up their own ventures. The company offers also number of trainings and workshops in areas related to its core activity.
The UWRC Ltd creates also a favourable condition for university – business cooperation. The company offers access to university infrastructure, laboratories and research teams managing several industrial contracts per year.
Since 2017, the UWERC Ltd participated in three editions of the Innovation Incubator Program (Innovation Incubator Plus, Innovation Incubator 2.0, Innovation Incubator 4.0) financed by the Polish Ministry of Science and Higher Education with the purpose to strengthen commercialisation processes at universities. The UWRC Ltd was always a consortium member with the University of Warsaw as the Leader and two other academic partners. The company was responsible for developing and implementation of an effective model for university spin-off creation and support for academic entrepreneurship. The most visible effect of the Program was support for establishment of 25 university spin-offs.
The UWRC Ltd is an active member of the Polish Alliance of University Knowledge Transfer Companies, which represents a community of more than 30 university spv from all Polish research universities.
